criterion_notes.c1: No. This is a macro water-resources and inter-basin raw-water transfer governance study examining the São Francisco River Integration Project (PISF — bulk aqueducts, pumping stations, canals, and strategic reservoirs) in Northeast Brazil (Exclusion Criterion 7: water-resource studies unrelated to household or community service access). Although the paper notes in regional background and discussion that semi-arid municipal supply systems and secondary structures are obsolete and poorly maintained—jeopardizing bulk water reaching end consumers—and that water distribution across localities favors wealthier areas, it does not empirically examine household or community drinking-water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2 taken in isolation, the paper does examine legal, institutional, and governance factors—specifically Brazil's National Water Resources Policy (Lei n. 9.433/1997), the PISF Management System (SGIB, Decreto n. 5.995/2006), the São Francisco River Basin Committee (CBHSF), Codevasf, and Ostrom's IAD rules-in-use. However, even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the overall full-text decision (plain_criterion2_decision) is still 'exclude' because the paper fails Criterion 1 and Criterion 4 as a river-basin / bulk raw-water resource governance study rather than a household or community service-access study. Under the active 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading, Criterion 2 is 'no': the governance mechanisms analysed are macro-level river-basin decision-making structures (federal-state voting concentration in SGIB, CBHSF subordination to CNRH, interagency fragmentation), bulk raw-water / irrigation O&M charges paid by states and authorized raw-water pumpers to Codevasf, and weak monitoring of raw-water canals crossing private properties—not rule-type mechanisms directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access (such as retail eligibility, tenure/documentation rules, household tariffs, disconnection/enforcement, or utility regulatory structure governing service access).
criterion_notes.c3: Yes. Qualitative empirical institutional case study applying Ostrom's IAD framework, using systematic documentary analysis (EIA, legislation, CGU/TCU audit reports) and primary conversational/open interviews conducted between 2015 and 2018 with federal and state water agencies, civil society researchers, one quilombola community, and two indigenous communities (including in loco fieldwork with the Pipipã), analysed in NVivo 11.
criterion_notes.c4: No. The empirically analysed outcomes are institutional and socio-environmental: territorial and interagency fragmentation, centralization of basin decision-making power in federal/state blocs (silencing grassroots and indigenous participation in SGIB/CBHSF), information asymmetry, destruction of approximately 1,250 km² of native Caatinga on Pipipã land, ontological conflicts over water, and high-level operational issues in strategic reservoirs and raw-water canals. No household or community water or sanitation service-access outcome (connection, retail affordability, household continuity, or utility exclusion) is empirically evaluated against a service-access rule.
criterion_notes.c5: Yes for its own qualitative case-study scope: the unit of analysis (the institutional 'action arena' of PISF water governance), qualitative study design (IAD case study with 2015–2018 interviews and document analysis), actor categories interviewed, institutional governance arrangements, and qualitative institutional/environmental outcomes are identifiable (though exact interviewee count is not reported, and no household service-access exposure-outcome pair exists).
criterion_notes.c6: Yes. Full text is in Portuguese, which is directly eligible without translation per Criterion 9.

evidence_quotes.quote: Este estudo busca compreender a gestão complexa da água analisando o sistema de governança das águas na área de influência do Projeto de Integração do Rio São Francisco (PISF), utilizando o Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) Framework de Elinor Ostrom

Dessa forma, a transposição conduz volumes adequados de água para os reservatórios estratégicos estaduais, sendo distribuída para as demais estruturas de abastecimento hídrico. No entanto, a ausência de manutenção dessas estruturas secundárias compromete os investimentos no projeto, uma vez que os eixos da transposição dependem da infraestrutura existente para garantir a chegada das águas aos consumidores finais.

As regras de limite e fiscalização do acesso às águas transpostas são frágeis (canais em propriedades privadas e usos difusos); a sustentabilidade financeira depende de tarifas e de uma oferta raramente excedente, abrindo espaço para conflitos

A estrutura do SGIB sofre com a existência de assimetria de poder e representação (Ostrom, 2007), porque a própria União e quatro governos estaduais formam um bloco decisor majoritário, com 50% de representação, o que dificulta o engajamento dos atores, a sua conscientização acerca de seus desafios e o aproveitamento de agentes de mudança.

Este estudo adota uma abordagem metodológica de natureza qualitativa (Godoi & Balsini, 2010), e a coleta de dados foi realizada entre os anos de 2015 e 2018, conforme a realização de entrevistas em formato conversacional, livre e padronizado aberto, com o objetivo de compreender os significados atribuídos aos problemas da governança da água (Creswell, 2010).

raw_response.exposure: Macro-institutional river-basin and inter-basin bulk water governance arrangements of the São Francisco River Integration Project (PISF) under Lei n. 9.433/1997 (PNRH), SGIB, CBHSF, CNRH, and Codevasf
raw_response.outcome: Institutional fragmentation, power and information asymmetries in basin governance committees, socio-environmental impacts (loss of 1,250 km² of Caatinga and cultural conflict with Pipipã indigenous community), and bulk reservoir/canal management challenges
raw_response.population_and_sample: Unit of analysis: institutional action arena of the PISF in Pernambuco/Northeast Brazil; qualitative interviews (2015–2018, exact N not reported) with representatives of MI, APAC/Prorural, Fundaj, Observatório das Águas, Compesa, Codevasf, one quilombola community in Garanhuns, and two indigenous communities in Ibimirim and Pesqueira
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E01 (Wrong topic — macro water-resource / inter-basin raw-water transfer governance unrelated to household or community water or sanitation service access, per Exclusion Criterion 7). Using Ostrom's IAD framework, interviews (2015–2018), and documentary analysis, the study examines the institutional governance arena of the São Francisco River Integration Project (PISF), focusing on federal-state power concentration in SGIB and CBHSF/CNRH, interagency fragmentation, bulk raw-water O&M charges and canal boundary monitoring, and socio-environmental impacts on native Caatinga and indigenous communities. Although it notes in passing that municipal supply systems and secondary reservoirs in the Semiárido are obsolete, it does not examine household or community water/sanitation service access (failing c1), does not analyse a rule-type mechanism directly governing service access under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 scope (failing narrow c2), and reports institutional/participatory and environmental outcomes rather than service-access outcomes (failing c4). Even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the paper remains excluded because it fails Criteria 1 and 4.
raw_response.study_design: Qualitative institutional case study using Ostrom's IAD framework (documentary analysis and open/conversational interviews, 2015–2018, analysed in NVivo 11)
